item.title: Version 1.2.8
item.description:
Pipit 1.2.8

Bug Fixes & Stability — Thank you for the feedback ❤️

This release fixes the transcription regressions reported after 1.2.7 and includes additional reliability improvements.

  • Long dictations — Fixed repeated or corrupted text that could begin around the 15-second mark, especially for multilingual transcription
  • CoreML stability — Fixed crashes during Parakeet model loading on affected Mac and macOS combinations
  • Recording tails — Improved end-of-dictation capture so the final words are less likely to be cut off

Word Corrections & Vocabulary

  • Safer corrections — Added stronger guards against replacing valid everyday words with unrelated learned aliases
  • Self-healing learning — Repeated corrections that users undo are automatically suppressed instead of continuing to recur
  • Pipeline reliability — Improved correction lifecycle tracking and fallback behavior

item.title: Version 1.2.7
item.description:
Pipit 1.2.7

Bug Fixes & Stability — Thank you for the feedback ❤️

This release is focused entirely on fixes and stability based on your reports.

  • History preview — Fixed the preview popover dismissing itself when you moved your mouse into it to scroll
  • Menu bar panel — Fixed the first click inside the history panel sometimes being swallowed and requiring a second press
  • Scroll detection — Fixed scroll events inside the preview being misread as list scrolls, closing the preview unexpectedly
  • Clipboard monitor — All pasteboard reads now happen off the main thread, reducing brief UI freezes
  • AX read timeouts — Accessibility reads now have hard timeouts, preventing hangs when a target app is slow to respond
  • Launch at startup — Fixed an edge case where toggling the setting could get stuck in a bad state
  • Onboarding — Improved the permission-skip flow so it's clearer what's optional vs. required

Word Corrections & Vocabulary

  • Less aggressive corrections — Words you remove from your dictionary no longer keep biasing transcription, so unintended auto-corrections happen far less often
  • Stale vocabulary cleared properly — "Reset Learned Corrections" now reliably clears terms learned from your edits, while keeping vocabulary from other sources (screen text, manual entry, imports)
  • Deletions stick — Dictionary deletions made while signed out now sync correctly on sign-in instead of quietly coming back
  • Performance — Bulk dictionary clears are faster and write to the sync queue once instead of once per word
